newsitem.title: ESTONIA: ESCO BIDS 700 MLN KROONS FOR ESTONIAN SHIPPING.
newsitem.headline: ESCO BIDS 700 MLN KROONS FOR ESTONIAN SHIPPING.

text.p: Esco Holdings on Tuesday confirmed it made a 700 million kroon bid for the privatisation of Estonian Shipping Company (Eesti Merelaevandus).
Esco Holding is held 50 percent by Norwegian Tschudi & Eitzen, 12 percent by Uhisinvesteeringud, the investment company of Uhispank , and 10 percent by Stanton Capital Corporation from the U.S.
Investment house Baltic Cresco has a 10 percent stake, the management of Estonian shipping company another 10 percent and eight percent belongs to EPEKS, an Estonian food production company.
ESCO Holding will invest 3.1 billion kroons over two years, chairman Olev Schults told a news conference.
"The sum will mostly be invested in the modernisation of shipping," he said.
Some 1.3 billion kroons will be invested in new cargo ships and another 1.36 billion in new passenger ships.
The business plan has two priorities for the shipping company: the first is the development of a highly competitive firm and the second to develop Estonia's transit trade, he added.
"The goal is to gain a leading position for Estonian shipping company in competition with Finland, Latvia and Lithuania," Schults said.
ESCO Holding also plans to start operations with tankers, which will create new opportunities for the development of Estonia's transit corridor, he added.
ESCO would also list the shipping company's shares on the stock exchanges in Tallinn and Oslo.
The privatisation agency will make a decision on the best bidder for the shipping company in June 18.
Another bidder, a consortium called Arbonale, is also competing for the privatisation of Estonian Shipping.

It was formed by Talinvest, Hansa Investments, N-Terminaal, Norwegian shipping company Navigator, Japanese investment bank Nomura and Hong Kong shipping company Jinhui Shipping and Transportation Ltd.
